n_board.text: Clicking a card opens a side drawer instead of a new page, so the board stays in view. Overdue and 'awaiting acceptance' are visible on the card.

n_concepts.text: Same idea, three connection shapes, all one colour: Flow (current), Route (precise right angle), Arc (bridge).

n_dash.text: Answer the queue without leaving the dashboard: approve, compare, accept inline. KPIs shrink to one strip.

n_logo.text: Flow, in one colour: two points — the customer and the crew — joined by one smooth curve. Near-black on light, white on dark, blue as an option.

n_phone.text: Suppliers' crews work on site: big touch targets, check-in first, time and photos in two taps, works offline.

n_status.text: One chip style per status (color + icon + word), one primary button per screen, empty states that say what to do next.

n_ws.text: Today the project page stacks schedule, cost, phases and 4 nav buttons. Proposal: tabs with counts, a sticky header and ONE 'next step' per role.

n_landing.text: Landing: one big promise, the real product in a window instead of stock photos, three steps, a bento grid of features, one call to action.

n_sd.text: Supplier dashboard: the invitation is the hero card with Accept / Decline — and shows whether the crew is free that week.

n_oc.text: Offer comparison: three columns with identical rows, weighted score, savings vs. baseline, revisions and compliance in plain words.

n_ir.text: Invoice review: the real document on the left, automatic checks and 'what changed' on the right, one big Approve.

n_pa.text: Phone approvals: managers approve invoices and time from the shop floor in one tap.
